correctness.rationale: The scientific claim is correct; the frozen proof needs a minor endpoint completion. The source reconstructs the delayed stage with the fresh stage of the current interval. With h=1 and f=-s times the delayed value this yields the stated companion map, including the nonzero triple ((1-s)c,c,c) for constant history c≠0. An independent exact monomial lift reproduces det(I-M)=sQ(s)/12, isolates one root in (9/8,7/6) and no others through 3/2, and gives the determinant -1270787/20155392 and positive cubic Routh margin 2104 at 7/6. The simple eigenvalue at s=0 has derivative -2. For s>0 the cone Perron eigenvalue is continuous and the adjoint positive eigenmatrix has invariant kernel under every stage companion. Stage differences yield e1 from any vector with nonzero third component, and the shift rows then generate all coordinates (or rule out a nonzero kernel confined to the plane x3=0). Thus the adjoint weight is definite and gives two-sided r(s)^j bounds for each nonzero initial. Use the determinant sign on the full (s*,3/2), not merely (s*,sqrt(2)) as written: this proves strict growth at sqrt(2), where the supplied Jensen lower bound alone is non-strict. For s≥3/2 the mean matrix has determinant ≥9/8, and Jensen plus the upper r(s)^j bound gives r(s)>1. The crossing is pinned from both sides by continuity. Increasing stage variance adds the positive rank-one map s^4 Δv X33 e1 e1^T; for positive variance the adjoint weight is definite and a nonzero positive eigenmatrix has X33>0 (otherwise the two shift equations force all its diagonal entries zero), giving strict increase. No simulated horizon was used as proof.
